brief.topic: A narrator compares the Pulse and Nova adapters used by Ravi and Meena, including their warnings, ratings and costs.
brief.register: Neutral everyday spoken Telugu, addressing the audience politely with మీరు

glossary.note: The blue adapter's model name; not a heartbeat

brief.numbers: Speak numbers, money and units naturally in Telugu script; retain exact values and uncertainty.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Ravi and Meena are testing two adapters before the repair.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: A technician called the blue model Pulse and the red model Nova.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Pulse charges the phone faster, but Nova uses less power.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Neither model repairs a damaged battery.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Ravi received the blue adapter, and Meena kept the red one.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: The blue adapter may overheat after about twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: He must unplug it if that happens, but she should keep hers connected.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That warning applies only to Ravi's adapter, not to both of them.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Hers is rated for twelve volts; his is rated for nine.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Those are voltage ratings, not charging times.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Meena paid two hundred and fifty rupees for Nova, including the cable.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Ravi paid the same amount for Pulse, but the cable was extra.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: He did not say that the extra cable was free.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: It might cost another fifty rupees, so his total is not confirmed.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: If both adapters stay cool, they can repeat the test tomorrow.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Until then, do not describe either model as proven safe.

semantic_expectations.check: Ravi and Meena test two adapters before the repair. Blue is Pulse, owned by Ravi; red is Nova, kept by Meena. Pulse charges faster, whereas Nova consumes less power. Do not swap either model or property.
Neither adapter repairs an already damaged battery; do not turn this into a positive repair claim or a claim that adapters damage batteries.

At the 6-line boundary, he/it refer to Ravi/the blue adapter, and she/hers to Meena/the red adapter. Unplugging is required only if overheating occurs. Meena's contrasting instruction remains to keep hers connected.
Overheating is possible, not certain. About twenty minutes is approximate, not an exact guarantee or a different number.

At the 8-line boundary, the warning is limited to Ravi's adapter. Her adapter is twelve volts, his nine volts. These are voltage ratings, explicitly not charging times. Correct pronouns may remain pronouns; naming their referents is not required.
Meena's Nova costs 250 rupees including its cable. Ravi paid the same 250 rupees for Pulse, with a separately charged cable. Do not say both cables were included or invent its price here.

At the second 6-line boundary, he/his still refers to Ravi and it to his extra cable. He did not claim it was free; preserve that reported-claim negation. Another 50 rupees is only a possibility, and his total remains unconfirmed; do not assert a definite 300-rupee total.
Repeating tomorrow is conditional on both adapters staying cool, not a promise. Neither model may yet be described as proven safe. Preserve the temporal limit and the negation.
Reuse Pulse/పల్స్ and Nova/నోవా consistently as model names, with natural Telugu suffixes allowed; do not translate Pulse as heartbeat.
